matt-support: Escalation: Acme webhook failing after model flip to rwinf-4b-2026-03. Their parser is throwing errors — looks like structured output (JSON mode) is sometimes emitted with extra wrapping and chunk boundaries that break parsing. P1 from CS. Sample error and a minimal repro below.

karen-cust: Customer error: "SyntaxError: Unexpected token , in JSON at position 452". Started ~2026-03-15 09:22 UTC. They see 500s on their side when our webhook forwards the generated JSON.

oliver-eng: Can you paste the request_id + route? Are they using stream=true + json_mode? If so we need the raw response (not the post-processed one). Also try a non-stream call to confirm.

matt-support: request_id: rwinf-req-0a1b2c3d. Route: /v1/generate/chat. Customer says they use streaming. Minimal repro (curl) they ran:

```bash
curl -s -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD" -d '{"model":"rwinf-4b-2026-03","stream":true,"json_mode":true,"input":"generate order JSON with items"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate | tee raw.txt
```

Raw stream chunks (sanitized):

```
data: {"chunk":"{\"order_id\":123,\"items\":["}

data: {"chunk":"{\"id\":\"sku-1\",\"qty\":2},"}

data: {"chunk":"{\"id\":\"sku-2\",\"qty\":1}]},
"}
```

Note how the wrapper and chunk boundaries leave an extra comma/brace in some boundaries. Customer's parser treats the combined stream as a single JSON message and hits the syntax error.

divya-ml: Sounds like the structured-output streaming encoder might have changed framing. Could be a regression in the chunk assembly after tokenization (we changed the chunk flush logic in the 2026-03 compile). Did the runtime change any downstream postprocess that wraps the top-level result?

runtime-bot: Canary swap to rwinf-4b-2026-03 completed at 2162490000.

oliver-eng: I can repro locally with stream=true when I stitch chunks naïvely. Will run a diff between rwinf-4b-2026-02 and -03 output framing. Opening ENG-10987 and assigning to eng-runtime. Suggested mitigation: revert canary for that model route until we vet framing.

matt-support: Revert requested and initiated. Customer has partial failures; they're asking about data loss and billing — flagged for priority.

sara-sre: Observed small latency bump on that canary. Also seeing increased 500s on the /webhook-ingest lambda around the same time. Adding tracing & request sampling to the route to capture raw stream payloads and response headers.

michael-product: Do we have telemetry on how many customers are hitting json_mode + stream for rwinf-4b? Need impact estimate before rollback. If rollback is necessary, delay next canary.

divya-ml: For quick mitigation, wrap a temporary server-side assembler in the webhook forwarder that accumulates chunks until a valid JSON parse succeeds (or timeouts). Also add a schema validation gate to drop/repair malformed top-level tokens. Not ideal long-term but reduces customer impact.

oliver-eng: Agreed. I'll post patch to the webhook proxy and link ENG-10987. Will mark for hotfix if rollback isn't clean.

matt-support: Thanks — I'll update the customer and create support-ticket #CS-5421 with the repro steps and raw.txt attached.

oliver-eng: Created ENG-10987 with logs and repro. ETA: initial triage in 2h.

matt-support: Appreciate it. Please ping when you have a build/rollback confirmed. :pray:
